name: The Church App
version: v2 · 2026-11-08 · moved onto the Grace Harbor practice church

persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Joy, 17, a student at Grace Harbor Church. Grace Harbor is not a real church - we invented it so you can test every part of this app safely. Your youth leader asked everyone to keep notes on the last few sermons (a sermon is the talk the pastor gives on Sunday). Today you want to write your notes in the church's app, and change the app back to light colours.

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called The Church App. You have never seen it, and that is fine. In about three minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.
First, the problem. In many churches, information is in too many places. The announcements are on a paper that people throw away. The Sunday talks are somewhere on YouTube. The calendar is on a wall.
The Church App puts all of it in one place, on every member's phone, with the church's own name on the front.

What you will see is a practice church called Grace Harbor. The church, its people, its sermons, its events and the prayers on its wall are all invented, so nothing you do here reaches anybody. That means you can use every part of it.
Who uses it? Church members, young and old, every week. The church office keeps it up to date from a phone.
Now let us walk through it slowly.
At the bottom of the screen there is a bar with six buttons: Home, Watch, Events, Prayer, Give and More. Tap one to move to that part of the app.

lines.t: Home is the first screen. At the top is a big picture of the latest message. In this app, a message means a sermon, the talk the pastor gives on Sunday. Tap the picture to open it.

lines: Below that you see the Sunday service times, the next events under Coming up, and the Discussion guide for this week.
Now tap Watch at the bottom. You see the Messages list. The newest message is at the top.

Above the list there is a row of buttons with the names of sermon series. A series is a group of sermons on one topic, for example Anchored, or Lifelines, or The Good Shepherd. Tap a series name to see only those messages. Tap All to see every message again.
Each message shows its title, the speaker, the Bible passage, and the date.
Tap a message to open it. You see a Watch message button, which opens the video on YouTube, and under it a box called My notes.
My notes is for your own notes: what stood out to you, or one thing to do this week. Just type. The app saves by itself after a moment, and says Saved. Your notes stay only on this phone.
Tap Back at the top left to return to the list. A message with notes now shows a small label: Notes saved.

On the Home screen there is also a button, My notes on this message. It opens Sermon Notes for the newest sermon, with more tools, like the Bible verses that were mentioned and questions to take home.
Events shows what is coming up at church. Old events disappear by themselves.

Prayer is where you can share a prayer request, and see the ones other people have shared. In a real church's app the Send button opens an email to the church office. Here it sends nothing at all, so please do send one, and make the words up.

Give opens the church's giving page. In this practice church the giving is switched off, so the button goes nowhere. Press it anyway, and tell us whether the screen made that clear before you pressed it.
More has the church's ministries, the team, and contact details. At the bottom there is Appearance. It has three choices. System follows your phone. Light makes the app white. Dark makes it black.
There is no Start fresh button in this app. Your notes stay until you delete the words yourself.
In the test, you will be a young church member taking sermon notes. Take your time, and say what confuses you. That is exactly what we want to hear.

challenge.intro: Now you are Joy, writing your sermon notes. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. Everything in this church is made up, so try anything you like - nothing reaches anybody. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open The Church App with the normal link: https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/church-demo/ . Everything in it is invented - Grace Harbor Church, its people, its sermons and its prayers - so nothing you do reaches anybody. This app has no Start fresh button, and you must NOT clear your browser's data (that would also erase your other test apps). Notes left from the script test can stay: these tasks only look at new notes on three older messages, and at the Appearance setting. (Verified 8 Nov against the practice church itself.)
challenge.challengeNote: The practice church at https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/church-demo/ has no Start fresh and no erase entry, so it cannot be emptied without wiping the whole jerrywins1.github.io site data (which would also erase every Daraja app). The challenge therefore asks for new notes on three messages the script test never opens - the script writes only on demoGH12, the newest - and for Appearance = Light, which the script leaves on Dark. Read off the demo in a browser on 8 Nov: a note saves to localStorage 'note:<message id>' as a JSON string, the message ids are demoGH01 to demoGH12, and Appearance saves to 'theme' as a JSON string. Unlike Immanuel's app, the prayer form and the giving button are safe here - the form saves on the phone and sends nothing, and Give online now is a dead link - so the test no longer has to warn anyone off them.

tasks.text: In the sermon series Lifelines, find Week 3, Honest prayer (by Dan Whitfield, Psalm 13). Write this note on it: Pray even when I am sad.
tasks.hint: Tap Watch at the bottom, then the Lifelines button above the list. There are four weeks; pick the one with the right title. The box is called My notes.

tasks.text: In the series The Good Shepherd, find Week 2, He calls them by name (by Pete Danvers, John 10:1–6). Write this note on it: He knows my own name.
tasks.hint: Watch, then the The Good Shepherd button. Three weeks; this is the middle one.

tasks.text: Find the message called The quiet work of faithfulness (by Tim Oyelaran, 1 Thessalonians 4:11–12). Write this note on it: Work quietly and mind my own business.
tasks.hint: It is not part of a series, so look under All, or under Standalone.

tasks.text: The script test left your app dark. Make it always light, even when your phone is dark.
tasks.hint: The setting is called Appearance, at the bottom of the More screen. It is a little menu. System is not the same as Light.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: the church's sermons, events, prayer and giving in one app on members' phones
you can find a sermon and keep your own notes on it, saved on your phone
the church office keeps it up to date; it carries the church's own name

daily.task: Open any message in The Church App and write one new line in your note on it.

explore.name: 🏠 Home
explore.find: It opens here. Or tap “Home” in the bar at the bottom.
explore.try: Tap the big latest-message picture. Tap Messages, Events, Prayer in the row of four. Tap “All events” and “📝 My notes on this message”. Tap Directions, look, come back.

explore.name: ▶️ One message
explore.find: On Home, tap the big picture, or tap any message on Watch.
explore.try: Type in “My notes”, go Back, open it again: is the note still there? Tap Share and look, don’t send. Tap Watch message, Listen, Guide, then come back.

explore.name: 📺 Watch
explore.find: Tap “Watch” in the bar at the bottom.
explore.try: Tap every series button at the top to filter the list. Open two messages. Look for the “Notes saved” mark. Tap “Full archive on YouTube” and “Listen to the podcast”.

explore.name: 🎙 Sermon Notes: During
explore.find: On Home, in “Discussion guide”, tap “📝 My notes on this message”.
explore.try: Tap “🎙 Record the sermon”, talk a little, then “⏹ Stop — the sermon is over”. Type a note and tap Add. Tap a 📖 verse. Tap the time on a note. Remove a note with ✕.

explore.name: ✨ Sermon Notes: After
explore.find: Inside Sermon Notes, tap the “✨ After” tab at the top.
explore.try: Play the recording. Tap a 📖 scripture. Tap “1 · Copy the sermon”, paste any text, tap “Save it”. Answer two questions. Tap “Share this sermon”: look, don’t send.

explore.name: 📚 My sermons library
explore.find: Inside Sermon Notes, tap “📚 Library” at the top.
explore.try: Tap Open on a saved sermon, then “‹ Back”. Try 🗑 on one test sermon only. Tap ✕ to close Sermon Notes.

explore.name: 📅 Events
explore.find: Tap “Events” in the bar at the bottom.
explore.try: Tap every group button at the top to filter the list. Read a few events. Tap “See all events on the website”, then come back.

explore.name: 🙏 Prayer
explore.find: Tap “Prayer” in the bar at the bottom.
explore.try: Tap “I prayed” on a request, then tap it again. Fill in a made-up name and a made-up request, tick “Keep it on my prayer list”, and tap “Send to the prayer team” - nothing leaves this practice church. Try “No email? Copy my request”.

explore.name: 💵 Give
explore.find: Tap “Give” in the bar at the bottom.
explore.try: Read the page. Tap “Give online now” - giving is switched off here, so say what happened and whether you expected it. Tap each way to give, and check the three links at the bottom.

explore.name: ⋯ More
explore.find: Tap “More” in the bar at the bottom.
explore.try: Tap Kids, Students, Adults, Get Involved. Look at “Our team”. Try a few Resources links. Change Appearance to Light, then Dark, then System.
